clue.text: Crazy person in middle of beach: "Back," he said

definitions.text: Crazy person in middle of beach: "Back," he said

parts.words: Crazy person in middle of beach: "Back," he said
parts.note: the legend of the Danish-English king who set his throne on the shore and ordered the incoming tide to go back, looking like a madman

explanation.surface: A lunatic standing on the sand shouts an order to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the famous story of the eleventh-century king who sat on the beach and commanded the waves to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of legend who commanded the tide to retreat is pictured here as an eccentric on the sands.

clue.text: Search far and wide to get players before a match

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
a bout is a contest or match

explanation.surface: Look everywhere to find a team before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' reads as a game, but here it is a boxing contest; 'players' are the actors in a production.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast about is to search widely in every direction for something.

clue.text: Group a number within ten set up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read from the bottom upwards, so reversed
within means the number abbreviation sits inside the word ten

parts.note: taken as written
NO is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Asks whether a band is a figure under ten.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'set up' turns the letters to read upwards, so the built word runs bottom to top in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine, especially nine musicians.

clue.text: Coming at the wrong moment, thin fog finds one at sea

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
the Roman numeral for one is I
the Med, the Mediterranean, is a sea

explanation.surface: A light haze lands someone out on the water at an awkward time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like it means confused or an anagram signal, but here it names the sea itself: MED for the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistimed happens at a poor or inconvenient moment, so the phrase is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Two snails going all out with ref being INVE scrupulously even-handed

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Two snails going all out with ref being INVE scrupulously even-handed': 'INVE' is garbled OCR (anagram of SNAIL SNAIL REF), and the scan is blank
annotationWithheld.clue: Two snails going all out with ref being INVE scrupulously even-handed

clue.text: A certain amount of Heathrow noise is projected into the air

indicators.note: A certain amount of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the din at London's main airport takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown means hurled, sent flying through the air.

clue.text: If one gets spliced then a celebratory drink is called for

definitions.text: If one gets spliced then a celebratory drink is called for

parts.words: If one gets spliced then a celebratory drink is called for
parts.note: the naval order to splice a particular rope was the old signal for an extra rum ration

explanation.surface: Getting married calls for a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spliced' suggests getting married, but the Royal Navy order 'splice the ...' meant an extra issue of rum for the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Splicing this rigging line was the Royal Navy signal for an extra tot of rum.

clue.text: Writer put little time into Hamlet, perhaps

indicators.note: into means the time letter goes inside the word for a Danish man

parts.note: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, so an example of a Dane
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: An author squeezed some brief time into Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' looks like the play or a small village, but it is the prince, a Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy is a famous writer.

clue.text: Heavy protection that's used by woman wanting son for husband

indicators.note: the woman wants a son in place of a husband, so the letter for son replaces the letter for husband

parts.note: a handbag is something a woman carries and uses

explanation.surface: A woman would rather have a boy than a spouse, and needs protecting.
explanation.walkthrough: H (husband) and S (son) are standard abbreviations; swapping them in HANDBAG gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandbags are heavy sacks piled up as protection against floods or gunfire.

clue.text: One watching out for another newspaper article to take shape

parts.note: the Guardian is a British newspaper
an is the indefinite article
to gel is to set or take shape

explanation.surface: A rival paper's piece starts to come together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' looks like it belongs with 'newspaper', a rival of the Times, but it ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a spirit or person who protects and watches over someone else.

clue.text: Call to court area right before game's starting in downpour

indicators.note: in tells us the letter goes inside the word for a downpour

parts.note: a downpour is heavy rain

indicators.note: starting means only the first letter of the word game is used

explanation.surface: A match is called off as rain sweeps across the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: G, the start of 'game's', goes inside RAIN to make RAGIN, after A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to summon them before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Business agent losing lead part for thespian

indicators.note: losing its lead part means the first letter of the agent word is dropped

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys and sells goods for others

explanation.surface: A commercial agent gives up the starring role to a stage performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead part' suggests a starring role in a play, matching 'thespian', but it means the first letter, F, which is removed from FACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a performer on the stage, from Thespis, the reputed first Greek dramatic player.

clue.text: Everything below a thrashing is permitted

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks things about, so these letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: Anything up to a beating is fair game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below a thrashing' reads like a limit on punishment, but 'thrashing' signals the anagram of BELOW A that follows ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allowable is permitted under the rules, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Old king is careless losing diamonds, servant reported back

indicators.note: losing tells us the suit letter is dropped from the word for careless

parts.note: dozy means slow-witted and careless
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
a man is a manservant

indicators.note: back tells us the word for reported runs the other way

parts.note: reported means said

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch carelessly mislays his jewels, according to his attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SAID into DIAS. The answer is the Greek name for the pharaoh Ramesses II, made famous by Shelley's sonnet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek name of the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II, a long-dead ruler, as in Shelley's poem.

clue.text: Sailor that waves may snatch?

indicators.note: waves toss and churn, so these letters are swirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks for a sailor who might be swept up by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' rearranges MAY SNATCH; the whole clue also describes a sailor at risk from waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman is someone who sails a yacht, a kind of sailor.

clue.text: Slough endlessly blights

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for slough loses its last letter

parts.note: a slough is a bog or marsh

explanation.surface: Slough, the English town, is relentlessly ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also a town west of London famously mocked by the poet Betjeman, which the surface leans on; here it means a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or damage, so mars and blights are verbs with the same sense.

clue.text: Way over mountains takes fifty years, unusually

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the street abbreviation stands above the mountains

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a range is a chain of mountains
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A mountain road takes an oddly long half-century to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely means in an odd or unusual way.

clue.text: Who's got a letter for himself and each The Tim of his closest siblings?

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Who's got a letter for himself and each The Tim of his closest siblings?': 'The Tim' is garbled OCR, and the scan is blank
annotationWithheld.clue: Who's got a letter for himself and each The Tim of his closest siblings?

clue.text: School food would be unable to continue after seconds

indicators.note: placed after the letter for seconds, the answer would make the word for stopped, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: someone stuck cannot carry on

explanation.surface: A school dinner so bad nobody could manage a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: S followed by the answer would give STUCK. Tuck is British school slang for snacks and sweets, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British boarding-school slang for food, especially sweets and snacks from the tuck shop.

clue.text: The building of the divine heart of Paris

definitions.text: The building of the divine heart of Paris

parts.words: The building of the divine heart of Paris
parts.note: the French name of the basilica on Montmartre translates as sacred heart, and it stands at the heart of Paris

explanation.surface: Asks for a famous Paris church dedicated to the holy heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Montmartre basilica's French name means holy heart, so a building of the divine heart in Paris describes it.

clue.text: Roughly paint a well-worn surface

indicators.note: roughly suggests a slapdash job, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Daub on some paint to give an aged finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges PAINT A.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is the sheen that forms on wood or metal with age and handling.

clue.text: Best-selling CDs reach a lot of shops

parts.note: to hit a target is to reach it
a parade is a British name for a row of shops

explanation.surface: Popular records turn up in many stores.
explanation.walkthrough: A PARADE is a British term for a short row of shops on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: The hit parade is the chart of the best-selling records of the week.

clue.text: When heads are cut from this mythical odious creature, maybe its new ones appear?

definitions.text: When heads are cut from this mythical odious creature, maybe its new ones appear?

indicators.note: cutting the head off each word leaves its second letter exposed at the front

explanation.surface: Lop the heads off a monster and fresh ones sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second letters of 'this mythical odious creature maybe', newly at the front once each first letter is gone. The whole clue also describes the many-headed monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lernaean monster Heracles fought grew two new heads for every one cut off.

clue.text: City rugby backs get suspension

indicators.note: backs tells us the abbreviation for rugby is turned round

parts.note: RU, rugby union, is the abbreviation for rugby
a ban is a suspension

explanation.surface: Defensive players at a city rugby club are banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like the rugby position, but it reverses RU to UR. 'City' works as an adjective, as in city life.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban means relating to a city, as in urban areas against rural ones.

clue.text: Element created to absorb oxygen

indicators.note: to absorb means the word for created takes the oxygen symbol inside it

parts.note: born means brought into being, created
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemical element made to take up oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is chemical element number 5, a metalloid.

clue.text: Reducing amplitude of oscillation heard as darned high-pitched ringing

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are spoken and what is entered sounds like them

parts.note: darned can be damn, and a high-pitched ringing is a ping

explanation.surface: A technical note on vibrations reduced to a dratted shrill tone.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, DAMN PING sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, damping is the reduction in amplitude of an oscillation by friction or resistance.

clue.text: Spend wildly planting one type of shrub round lake

indicators.note: round means the shrub word goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: spurge is a kind of euphorbia shrub

explanation.surface: Throw money about by landscaping a garden around a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurge (euphorbia) is a family of plants with milky sap; L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend extravagantly, so it means the same as spending wildly.

clue.text: Almost cancel unstarted car race as MOTs must be renewed

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for cancel is dropped

parts.note: to annul is to cancel

indicators.note: unstarted means the word for a car race loses its first letter

parts.note: a rally is a car race on public roads

explanation.surface: Scrap a car race before it begins, since vehicle checks must be redone.
explanation.walkthrough: An MOT is the compulsory yearly roadworthiness test for cars in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The British MOT vehicle test must be repeated every year, so it is renewed yearly.

clue.text: Wasps are so near

definitions.meaning: wasps are insects with stings, so they are full of stings
near is old-fashioned for mean or tight with money

explanation.surface: Wasps are close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' looks like close, but it is the old sense of miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy describes something with stings, and also means mean with money, as near does.
